title: mean of many floats loses precision
description: mean(values) computes the arithmetic mean of a list of floats. It returns a value that is slightly off for large inputs with values of very different magnitudes — the result fails an exact-equality precision check. Make it numerically exact.

hidden_tests.test_stats_fp.py:
import math

from stats_fp import mean


def test_simple():
    assert mean([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]) == 2.0


def test_two():
    assert mean([0.5, 1.5]) == 1.0


def test_precision_mixed_magnitudes():
    # Naive left-to-right summation loses low-order bits here; the exact mean
    # must match math.fsum-based accumulation bit-for-bit.
    vals = [1e16, 1.0, -1e16, 1.0] * 2500  # 10000 values
    expected = math.fsum(vals) / len(vals)
    assert mean(vals) == expected


def test_precision_small_then_large():
    vals = [0.1] * 1000000 + [1e16, -1e16]
    expected = math.fsum(vals) / len(vals)
    assert mean(vals) == expected
